rv.q: This “Gypsy” spends much of its time in such intoxicating air.
This is not your everyday canned tuner; in this production it’s an incisively acted musical play with as much emotional resonance as showbiz pizzazz.
But I say she carries the burden gloriously.
At Tuesday's press preview, at least, her performance felt rushed, tightly wound and overdone.
In a performance that’ll have musical comedy fanatics buzzing for months, LuPone executes a show-biz finish to end all finishes.
The show wows you with dazzling skill, but ultimately moves you only slightly.

cn.t: LuPone's laser-focused, ferocious Rose commands this revival with controlled hysteria and show-stopping power, though the production itself feels somewhat stripped-down and old-fashioned around her tour-de-force performance.

vs.sum: The St. James Theatre offers good sightlines for most seats, though the lack of a solid rake can be an issue if someone tall sits in front of you. The sound quality is generally good, but the tight legroom can be uncomfortable for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic and grand interior, while facilities are average with standard amenities.

acc.note: No steps from sidewalk to Orchestra. No elevator. Mezzanine up 29 steps, Balcony up 76 steps.
